title: Dodge Coronet Engines by Year (1949–1976)
description: Every factory engine in the Dodge Coronet and Super Bee by year: Red Ram Hemi V8s of the 1950s, then the 383 Magnum, 440 Six Pack and 426 Hemi of 1965–1976.
intro: Dodge used the Coronet name on its full-size cars from 1949 to 1959 and on its mid-size cars from 1965 to 1976. The Super Bee (1968–1970) and R/T were Coronet models, and the trims column marks the engines only they got.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The early Coronet used Dodge's 230 flathead six and, from 1953, the Red Ram Hemi V8, later joined by wedge-head V8s up to the 383. The D-500 packages were Dodge's performance engines.
The mid-size Coronet ran from the slant six to the 426 Street Hemi. The R/T came with the 440 Magnum, the Super Bee with the 383 Magnum, and the 440 Six Pack arrived during 1969. Ratings are gross.
The last Coronets were mainly sedans and wagons, with the slant six, 318, 360 and 400. Ratings are SAE net from 1972.
